chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Dating the Casbah and Oasis years; the two record bands
summary: Lee and Willard work out dates for Sarah Vaughan's Black Coffee, Lee's move to Nat in 1953, and the late-1940s record band.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You know, that was almost, like, '50, wasn't it?
Could have been ... but it really should not have been, because it was at the Casbah and at the 50's
And I worked at The Oasis, and then I joined Nat in '53, see?
It seemed tome that "Black Coffee" was popular in 1950, but maybe I am wrong.

It probably was, and you know, I'll tell you how I arrive at things chronologically, but it's tough for me to get them, but I do know that -- and during the same time June Christie worked out there. June Christie worked at The Casbah. You know where the Casbah was? It was near Florence Blvd. on Figaro.

So that band was out there, and that was an awfully good band. But now whenever it was, it was -- I'll tell you one thing -- it was during the record band also because again, we had the record band at that time. Because I know when I used to go record the black market ... a lot of guys made a lot of money then in the record business.
Why do you associate that with "Black Coffee"? Because the record band was earlier, wasn't it? Now wait a minute.
No, you're talking about -- there were 2 record bands.
You're talking about the one during the war, you know, because you know why they banned it disbanded then. But
this one came in the late 40's. I'm positive it was the late '40's.
That's right. That's when Eden Ahaz did 'Nature Boy' and all the voices. -- --
And another reason I know it was, was because, oh yes, that was like, '48 or '49, yeah, it was somewhere along in there. Right. Because they used to -- Capital was right there.
